edits.old: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation carries a stroke risk similar to persistent AF, so it is assessed in the same way; female sex on its own is no longer regarded as a reason to anticoagulate, which is why the sex category was dropped to give CHA₂DS₂-VA.

edits.old: A. Tablet colour preference is not a safety check. C. Blood group does not affect antibiotic choice. D. Hand dominance has no bearing on prescribing. E. The pharmacy address is administrative and does not affect safety.
edits.new: A. Kidney function matters for some antibiotics in people with known renal disease or at the extremes of age, but a young woman with no renal history does not need results before every prescription. C. Previous cultures help when infections recur or fail to respond, but they are not a safety check needed for every prescription. D. Other regular medicines should be reviewed where relevant, but allergy status is the check required before any prescription. E. Recent travel matters when a resistant organism is suspected, which is not the situation here.

edits.old: E, Her usual pharmacy — it is needed to send the prescription electronically, but it is an administrative detail rather than a safety check.
edits.new: D, Her other regular medicines — checking for interactions is good practice and the option is easy to over-think, but the question asks which detail must always be confirmed, and a recorded allergy is the prerequisite for prescribing.
